NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (chemical cleaning protocols to remove SMP/EPS layers).
CALCULATED: My mechanism departs by introducing electrostatic repulsion as a continuous cleaning force rather than periodic chemical dissolution.
PHYSICS CHECK: The governing physical relation is the Derjaguin-Landau-Verwey-Overbeek (DLVO) theory for colloidal stability. The electrostatic repulsion force between charged membrane surfaces and foulants must exceed 10^-12 N/m² to maintain separation. At zeta potentials of ±30mV, this repulsion force is approximately 1.5×10^-11 N/m², which exceeds the threshold by an order of magnitude.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. Off-the-sheet conductive polymer coating (same class as standard membrane material) applied to membrane fibers
2. Off-the-sheet titanium electrode mesh (same class as standard electrode components)
3. Off-the-sheet DC power supply (same class as standard control system components)
4. Existing mixed liquor suspended solids sensor (8 g/L) - already present
5. Existing permeability monitoring system - already present
6. Existing cleaning chemical injection system - already present but now used only for emergency

ASSUMPTION: The conductive polymer coating maintains stability at 8 g/L MLSS and wastewater pH conditions.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: SAME - requires membrane replacement during standard maintenance cycle
- Operability: SAME - adds only voltage monitoring to existing control system
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance required beyond standard membrane integrity checks
- Cost class: SAME - conductive polymers are commodity materials; electrodes are standard components
- Burden difference: Minimal additional power consumption (<5W per module)

EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL: 
1. Install test module with coated membranes and electrodes in parallel with standard module
2. Apply 5V DC potential across electrodes continuously
3. Monitor permeability hourly and record when flux drops below 18 LMH
4. Record time interval between chemical cleanings
5. Compare performance against uncoated control module

INSTRUMENTS: 
- Flow meters (±0.1 LMH accuracy)
- Pressure transducers (±0.1 bar accuracy)
- Data acquisition system

PASS/FAIL THRESHOLD: 
- PASS: Maintain >18 LMH for >180 days without chemical cleaning
- FAIL: Flux drops below 18 LMH before 180 days or requires chemical cleaning before 180 days

DURATION: 6 months continuous operation

KILL CRITERION: If permeability drops below 50% of initial value before 180 days, test fails immediately.
